title_en: Tang Guowei v. Guangzhou Haishun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Changchun Gaosida Biotechnology Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over execution objection by a third party
ruling_gist_en: The authenticity, validity, and performance of a housing sale contract concluded between a third party (person not party to the execution) and the judgment debtor fall within the scope of matters that should be tried in the third party's execution objection lawsuit. If, outside the execution objection lawsuit, the third party and the judgment debtor separately initiate another lawsuit regarding the validity, continued performance, etc., of the subject matter of execution, there is suspicion of collusive litigation, which may harm the interests of the execution applicant. Therefore, such separate lawsuit should not proceed, and the execution objection lawsuit shall not be suspended due to the separate lawsuit.

full_text_en:
Tang Guowei v. Guangzhou Haishun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Changchun Gaosida Biotechnology Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over a third-party enforcement objection lawsuit

【Ruling Summary】

The authenticity, validity, and performance of a house purchase and sale agreement entered into between a third party and the enforcement respondent are all matters that should be tried in the third-party enforcement objection lawsuit. If, apart from the enforcement objection lawsuit, the third party and the enforcement respondent separately initiate other proceedings concerning the validity or further performance of the contract with respect to the subject matter of enforcement, there is a suspicion of collusive litigation, which may harm the interests of the enforcement applicant. Therefore, such separate proceedings should not be continued, and the enforcement objection lawsuit shall not be stayed pending the outcome of those separate proceedings.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling

(2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 3075

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Tang Guowei, male, born April 11, 1968, Han Chinese, residing in Haizhu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Pan Xiaoyong, lawyer of Guangdong Yongtong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Guangzhou Haishun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 144, Xingang West Road, Haizhu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Peng Shengtao, General Manager of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Changchun Gaosida Biotechnology Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 602, Unit 1, Building 5, Dongyuan Community, Taoyuan Road, Nanguan District, Changchun, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Yuan Chenliang, Chairman of the Company.

Applicant for retrial Tang Guowei, in the case of the third-party enforcement objection lawsuit against Respondents Guangzhou Haishun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haishun Company) and Changchun Gaosida Biotechnology Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gaosida Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2015) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 39 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Guangdong High Court), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to examine this case, and the examination has now been concluded.

Tang Guowei applied for retrial to this Court on the following grounds: (1) The original trial findings of fact were erroneous. On March 3, 2009, Tang Guowei and Haishun Company signed a House Purchase and Sale Agreement, under which Tang Guowei agreed to purchase from Haishun Company the property located at Shop 102, Building 9, Shunhua Street, Xingang West Road, Haizhu District, Guangzhou, for a price of RMB 1,408,260. Tang Guowei paid the purchase price to Haishun Company on the same day, and Haishun Company delivered the property to Tang Guowei on the same day. However, due to reasons attributable to Haishun Company, the transfer of title was not completed. Haishun Company confirmed the foregoing facts. Without any contrary evidence, the Guangdong High Court completely denied the facts confirmed by the parties and confirmed by effective civil judgments and arbitration awards by way of inference, which directly led to an erroneous application of law and should be corrected in accordance with law. (2) The second instance trial should have been stayed but was not, seriously damaging the lawful rights and interests of Tang Guowei, and the procedure was illegal. The result of the validity of the House Purchase and Sale Agreement between Tang Guowei and Haishun Company directly affects the outcome of this case. Therefore, this case should have been stayed pending the entry into effect of the judgment in the lawsuit concerning the validity of the House Purchase and Sale Agreement. The second instance court, knowing that the lawsuit concerning the validity of the House Purchase and Sale Agreement was still being heard, did not stay the proceedings in this case, which was procedurally illegal. Accordingly, Tang Guowei applied for retrial pursuant to Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

This Court holds that this case is a third-party enforcement objection lawsuit. Based on the grounds raised by Tang Guowei in his application for retrial, the main issues to be examined in this case are: first, whether the second instance procedure was illegal and whether the proceedings should have been stayed; and second, whether Tang Guowei enjoys a civil right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement with respect to the property in question.

(I) Whether the second instance procedure was illegal and whether the proceedings should have been stayed

With respect to an enforcement objection lawsuit, according to Article 312 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, if a third party simultaneously raises a claim for confirmation of his or her right, the people's court may render a ruling on that claim together in its judgment. In this case, the claims raised by the third party Tang Guowei included a claim for confirmation of right, namely, a request to confirm that the property in question is owned by him. Therefore, whether the House Purchase and Sale Agreement between Tang Guowei and Haishun Company is authentic, its validity, and its performance are all matters that should be tried as part of the confirmation of right aspect of this enforcement objection lawsuit.

According to the facts found by the original trial, after the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou Intermediate Court) seized the property in question on August 12, 2009, Tang Guowei, on March 18, 2010, as plaintiff, separately filed a lawsuit against Haishun Company as defendant seeking confirmation that the House Purchase and Sale Agreement was valid. Thereafter, on July 2, 2010, Tang Guowei raised an objection to the enforcement proceedings concerning the property in question. After the Guangzhou Intermediate Court rejected his enforcement objection, Tang Guowei filed this enforcement objection lawsuit. It is not difficult to see that the separate lawsuit filed by Tang Guowei seeking confirmation that the House Purchase and Sale Agreement was valid was for the purpose of preparing evidence for his enforcement objection and enforcement objection lawsuit. However, the outcome of that separate lawsuit, filed after the seizure of the property in question, clearly has an interest for the enforcement applicant Gaosida Company, which applied for the seizure of the property. Without adding Gaosida Company as a third party in those proceedings, the separate litigation between Tang Guowei and Haishun Company raises a suspicion of collusive litigation and may harm the interests of Gaosida Company. Moreover, the requirements for burden of proof differ between an enforcement objection lawsuit and a lawsuit for confirmation of a valid contract. Therefore, after this enforcement objection lawsuit was filed, the separate lawsuit filed by Tang Guowei seeking confirmation that the House Purchase and Sale Agreement was valid should not have been continued, and the facts concerning whether the House Purchase and Sale Agreement is authentic, its validity, and its performance should be determined and adjudicated in this enforcement objection lawsuit. In conclusion, the second instance trial in this case did not need to rely on the outcome of the separate lawsuit for confirmation of the validity of the House Purchase and Sale Agreement, and there was no need to stay the proceedings. The second instance procedure was not illegal.

(II) Whether Tang Guowei enjoys a civil right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement with respect to the property in question

When a third party brings an enforcement objection lawsuit, the third party bears the burden of proof to establish that he or she enjoys a substantive right sufficient to preclude enforcement over the subject matter of enforcement. Even if the enforcement respondent admits the claims of the third party, the third party's burden of proof is not relieved, in order to prevent collusion between the third party and the enforcement respondent that may harm the interests of the enforcement applicant. In this case, although Haishun Company confirmed the facts alleged by Tang Guowei, this does not relieve Tang Guowei of his burden of proof. In conjunction with Article 17 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Seizure, Impoundment and Freezing of Property in Civil Enforcement by People's Courts, in this case, for Tang Guowei to claim a civil right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement, he must provide evidence establishing that he has satisfied the relevant requirements, such as payment of the purchase price and actual possession of the property.

In this case, first, Tang Guowei failed to provide evidence establishing that he had paid the purchase price of over RMB 1.4 million. For Tang Guowei to claim that he had paid the purchase price, he must first establish that a house purchase and sale relationship existed between him and Haishun Company. However, the House Purchase and Sale Agreements produced by Tang Guowei at the time of filing the complaint at first instance and at the time of evidence exchange were inconsistent, and his explanations were clearly contradictory. Therefore, the original trial's refusal to recognize the authenticity of the agreement was not improper. Moreover, Tang Guowei did not provide any payment receipt for his payment claim. Even if his income was considerable, a claim that a lump sum of over RMB 1.4 million was paid in cash is clearly inconsistent with customary practices for large-value fund transactions in real life. Second, Tang Guowei failed to provide evidence establishing that he had actually taken possession of the property in question. During the first instance investigation of whether the property in question was leased by Tang Guowei to Yang Jun, Tang Guowei did not mention the Supplementary Agreement and the important fact of prepaid rent that he had submitted in the arbitration case No. (2015) Sui Zhong An Zi No. 447 of the Guangzhou Arbitration Commission. The process of rent payment from Yang Jun to Tang Guowei found by the arbitration award also clearly contradicted the statements made by Tang Guowei in the first instance of this case. Furthermore, according to the analysis of the second instance court, the authenticity of the Property Management Contract submitted by Tang Guowei as evidence of his actual possession of the property in question could not be confirmed, and he failed to provide property management fee invoices corresponding to the address of the property in question and the amount stipulated in the contract. Therefore, even though the relevant arbitration award confirmed the fact that Tang Guowei had leased the property in question to Yang Jun, given that the statements and relevant evidence submitted by Tang Guowei in this case before that arbitration proceeding clearly contradicted the facts found by the arbitration award, the original trial's refusal to accept the finding of the arbitration award was not improper. Moreover, the result of that arbitration award also clearly has an interest for enforcement applicant Gaosida Company, which applied for the seizure of the property in question. Since Gaosida Company did not participate in the arbitration, the separate arbitration between Tang Guowei and Haishun Company raises a suspicion of collusive arbitration. Based on the foregoing analysis, since Tang Guowei does not satisfy the requirements for enjoying a civil right or interest sufficient to preclude enforcement, the original trial's judgment dismissing his claim for exclusion of enforcement was not improper.

In conclusion, the application for retrial by Tang Guowei does not satisfy the circumstances set forth in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to Article 204, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 395, paragraph 2, of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, it is ruled as follows:

The application for retrial by Tang Guowei is rejected.
